The stock is down 18.6% over 5 days and 38.9% over 20, 73% off its 52-week high and 2% above the low; 20-day realised vol is 145% (sealed baseline). Front-week (11-27) straddle 11.9%, or 5.26% net of ordinary vol. 25-delta skew is +13 vol points toward puts while put/call open interest is 0.22 (baseline). Over the prior 7 prints the median absolute reaction was 6.1%, 4 of 7 up. Consensus for FQ4 (Jul-Sep): EPS -$0.26 (Chartmill; revenue $137M, revenue estimate cut 20.7% in 3 months) or -$0.37 (Benzinga; revenue $126-131M). Monthly production updates covered July-September, so mining output is already public: September 529 BTC, 36.0 EH/s average, 13,530 BTC held at 9/30. There is no forward guide. Positioning: 78.7M shares short at the 10-30 settlement, 4.6 days to cover (Nasdaq), about 29% of roughly 270M shares (my arithmetic from the Q3 EPS share count), partly convert hedges. Sentiment and price action: BTC is at $59.9k, down 25% in a month (Fortune, Yahoo). The Texas governor-elect backs a data-centre pause, KBW downgraded, Bernstein cut its target to $11, and the 11-20 AI-miner selloff took CLSK -16%, IREN -18% and CIFR -16%. At about $1.39B market cap against about $810M of BTC at spot, the price gives roughly zero credit for the 885 MW Texas exclusivity.
view: This print is mostly known before it lands. Quarterly mining revenue follows from the published monthly production times the average BTC price of roughly $70-80k, so revenue lands near the $126-137M consensus. GAAP EPS will probably be strongly positive against a -$0.26 to -$0.37 consensus. BTC rose about 39% in the quarter ($60.1k to $83.5k), which on about 13.5k BTC is roughly a +$316M fair-value gain (my arithmetic). That is mechanical and visible to everyone, and in Aug-2025 a $257M GAAP profit still drew a -6% reaction, so the headline EPS is not the line. The stock trades on the AI/HPC story and on BTC. The live question is the Texas exclusivity with the Sandersville tenant. It started on 2026-07-14, management said such windows run 30-120 days and was still calling it intact on 08-06, and it is now 133 days old. Since then Abbott ordered an ERCOT/PUCT audit, a pause-backing governor was elected, and no 8-K has been filed since 09-25. The call therefore has to say whether the window was signed, extended or lapsed. The price, near BTC value plus little, already assumes Texas is dead or delayed, so an extension or a signing would be upside and a lapse partly priced. Against that, BTC at $60k makes mining cash flow near zero against $179M a year of interest on the 7.875% notes. Management may talk about selling BTC, curtailing hashrate or impairments, and sector tape and overnight BTC moves (145% realised vol) will drown most of the release's signal by the next open. In this tape, peer prints (CIFR about flat, IREN recovered after hours, CORZ -11% on its report day) did not show a consistent direction. I lean slightly up, from the oversold, short-heavy setup and the low bar on Texas, but not far enough from a coin flip to act.
unpriced: Possibly the Texas exclusivity outcome: at about 1.7x BTC holdings the price holds almost nothing for 885 MW, so any credible extension or a definitive lease would be upside the price does not hold. But I could not find a dated public trace since 08-06 (no 8-K, no reported conference remarks) showing which way it went, so this is an asymmetry in the payoff, not evidence of direction.

recommendation.reason: The numbers in the release are already known from the monthly updates and the BTC price, and the large GAAP profit from fair-value marks is mechanical. The one undecided line is the Texas exclusivity status, and I found no public trace of its outcome. Short interest and the oversold tape tilt the payoff slightly up, but BTC overnight and the sector selloff dominate the next-open window, so no mechanism reaches 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A definitive Texas lease or a written extension of the exclusivity with the same tenant would make it a clear up. A disclosed lapse, a Texas/Sandersville delay, or a BTC fire-sale/curtailment plan alongside a going-concern-style liquidity discussion would make it down.

self_critique: The case for down is strong. BTC is in a sharp downtrend ($60k), and the stock's next-open move is mostly BTC and sector beta, which has been relentlessly negative. Mining at today's hashprice probably burns cash against about $179M of annual note interest, so the call may bring BTC sales, curtailment or a weaker liquidity picture. A 133-day-old exclusivity that has not converted while Texas politics turned hostile is more likely to have lapsed than been signed. The case for up is also real: the stock is near BTC value with ~29% of shares short, and one reassuring Texas or Georgia line could squeeze it. Each side has a mechanism and I have evidence of the outcome for neither, so 53 is about right and no action is warranted.
approach_notes: P4 and P6 helped. Finding the line (Texas exclusivity) and separating the mechanical fair-value EPS from what the stock trades on kept me off a headline-beat trap. P3's 'freshest data' hit a wall: the company stopped monthly updates and filed no 8-K since September, so there was no fresh company trace. For a BTC-beta name the playbook says nothing about how to treat overnight beta that swamps the release inside the scored window.
